role.instructions: The input state contains a user's prompt to a coding agent, broken into numbered segments. Determine the role of item [{{item}}] within the request.

criteria.context: Requests no standalone work: background info, goal framing ("i want to add X", "can you:", "we use bun", current behavior), or a lead-in whose directive governs every entry listed beneath it ("update these docs:", "add X for these providers:").
criteria.task: Requests actual work: an edit, bugfix, design, analysis, or answer — including a sub-detail or constraint for that work, or a single entry covered by a lead-in.
criteria.wrapup: A concluding pass across the entire request that runs after all other items: running the test suite or verification checks, committing, or updating docs/changelog overall.

coupled.instructions: The input state contains a user's prompt to a coding agent, broken into numbered segments. Two items are coupled when one worker needs to handle them together or sequentially: they modify the same file, function, command, or module (items targeting the same file or module remain coupled even when their edits differ); one depends on the other's output, design, choice, or newly introduced API; one renames or refactors code touched by the other; or one merely clarifies, narrows, or specifies the other. Items are independent if separate workers could execute them concurrently in the same checkout without blocking on or clobbering one another. Are items [{{a}}] and [{{b}}] coupled?
